chapters.title: Introduction to React
chapters.description: Understanding what React is and why it is used

pages.title: What is React?
pages.content: React is a JavaScript library used for building user interfaces. It was developed by Facebook and is widely used for building fast, scalable, and interactive web applications. React allows developers to create reusable UI components and efficiently update the user interface using a virtual DOM.

quiz.question: Who developed React?
quiz.explanation: React was developed by Facebook (Meta).

pages.title: Why Use React?
pages.content: React helps developers build modern web applications efficiently. It uses a component-based architecture where UI elements are reusable. React also uses a virtual DOM which improves performance by updating only necessary parts of the UI.
keyPoints: Fast UI updates with Virtual DOM

quiz.question: What improves UI performance in React?
quiz.explanation: React uses Virtual DOM to efficiently update the UI.

pages.title: Setting Up React Project
pages.content: React applications can be created using tools like Create React App or Vite. These tools set up the development environment and provide a ready-to-use project structure.
pages.exampleCode:
npm create vite@latest react-app

cd react-app

npm install

npm run dev

quiz.question: Which command starts a Vite project?
quiz.explanation: npm create vite@latest creates a new Vite React project.

chapters.title: JSX
chapters.description: Understanding JSX syntax used in React applications

pages.title: What is JSX?
pages.content: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It is a syntax extension used in React to describe what the UI should look like. JSX allows developers to write HTML-like code inside JavaScript. React converts JSX into JavaScript objects which are then rendered to the DOM.

quiz.question: What does JSX stand for?
quiz.explanation: JSX stands for JavaScript XML.

pages.title: Embedding JavaScript in JSX
pages.content: JSX allows JavaScript expressions to be embedded inside curly braces {}. This makes it possible to dynamically display values inside the UI.
keyPoints: Variables can be displayed in JSX

quiz.question: Which symbol is used to embed JavaScript in JSX?
quiz.explanation: Curly braces {} are used to embed JavaScript in JSX.

pages.title: JSX Rules
pages.content: JSX has certain rules that must be followed. JSX elements must return a single parent element. All tags must be properly closed, and class attributes should use className instead of class.
keyPoints: JSX must return one parent element

quiz.question: Which attribute replaces 'class' in JSX?
quiz.explanation: JSX uses className instead of class.

pages.title: JSX Expressions
pages.content: JSX supports JavaScript expressions such as arithmetic operations, function calls, and conditional expressions. This allows dynamic rendering of content.
keyPoints: Functions can be called inside JSX

quiz.question: Which operation is allowed inside JSX expressions?
quiz.explanation: JSX supports variables, functions, and calculations.

pages.title: JSX Example Component
pages.content: Below is a simple React component using JSX to display dynamic content. JSX makes UI development easier and more readable.

quiz.question: Where is JSX mainly used?
quiz.explanation: JSX is used inside React components to define UI.

chapters.title: Components
chapters.description: Understanding React components and how they build user interfaces

pages.title: What are Components?
pages.content: Components are the building blocks of a React application. A component is a reusable piece of UI that can be used multiple times throughout the application. React applications are typically made by combining many small components together.
keyPoints: React applications are built using components

quiz.question: What are the building blocks of React applications?
quiz.explanation: React applications are built using reusable components.

pages.title: Functional Components
pages.content: Functional components are JavaScript functions that return JSX. They are the most commonly used type of component in modern React applications. Functional components are simple, readable, and support React Hooks.
keyPoints: Most commonly used in modern React

quiz.question: What does a functional component return?
quiz.explanation: Functional components return JSX.

pages.title: Class Components
pages.content: Class components are ES6 classes that extend React.Component. They were commonly used in earlier React versions. Class components can manage state and lifecycle methods but are now mostly replaced by functional components with Hooks.

quiz.question: Which method must exist in class components?
quiz.explanation: Class components must contain the render() method.

pages.title: Reusable Components
pages.content: One of the main advantages of React is component reusability. A single component can be reused in multiple places within the application, making development faster and code easier to maintain.
keyPoints: Components can be reused multiple times

quiz.question: What is the advantage of reusable components?
quiz.explanation: Reusable components reduce development time.

pages.title: Component Example
pages.content: Below is a simple React application that uses multiple components to build a UI. Each component handles a specific part of the interface.
keyPoints: Each component has a specific purpose
Components can be combined to build UI

quiz.question: Which syntax is used to render a component?
quiz.explanation: Components are rendered using the <Component /> syntax.

chapters.title: Props
chapters.description: Passing data between React components using props

pages.title: What are Props?
pages.content: Props (short for properties) are used to pass data from one component to another in React. They allow parent components to send values to child components. Props make components dynamic and reusable.
keyPoints: Used to pass data between components
Passed from parent to child components

quiz.question: What does props stand for?
quiz.explanation: Props is short for properties.

pages.title: Passing Props
pages.content: Props are passed to components as attributes similar to HTML attributes. The child component receives these values as parameters.

quiz.question: How are props passed to components?
quiz.explanation: Props are passed as attributes similar to HTML attributes.

pages.title: Props Destructuring
pages.content: Props destructuring allows developers to directly extract values from props instead of writing props.name multiple times. This makes the code cleaner and easier to read.

quiz.question: What is the advantage of props destructuring?
quiz.explanation: Destructuring improves code clarity and readability.

pages.title: Default Props
pages.content: Default props allow components to have default values when no props are provided. This ensures components still work even if some props are missing.

quiz.question: What happens when a prop is not provided?
quiz.explanation: Default props provide fallback values.

pages.title: Props Example Component
pages.content: Below is an example where a component receives multiple props and displays them in the UI.

quiz.question: Where do props come from?
quiz.explanation: Props are passed from parent components.

chapters.title: State
chapters.description: Managing dynamic data inside React components

pages.title: What is State?
pages.content: State is a built-in object in React that allows components to store and manage dynamic data. When the state of a component changes, React automatically re-renders the component to reflect the updated UI.

quiz.question: What happens when state changes?
quiz.explanation: When state changes, React re-renders the component.

pages.title: useState Hook
pages.content: The useState hook is used in functional components to create and manage state. It returns an array containing the current state value and a function to update the state.
keyPoints: Returns state value and update function

quiz.question: Which hook is used to manage state?
quiz.explanation: useState is used to create and manage state.

pages.title: Updating State
pages.content: State can be updated using the setter function returned by useState. When the setter function is called, React updates the state and re-renders the component.

quiz.question: Which function updates state?
quiz.explanation: The setter function returned by useState updates state.

pages.title: State vs Props
pages.content: Props are used to pass data between components, while state is used to manage data inside a component. Props are read-only, whereas state can be updated using setter functions.
keyPoints: Props are passed from parent to child

quiz.question: Which one is read-only in React?
quiz.explanation: Props are read-only.

pages.title: State Example Component
pages.content: Below is an example where state is used to update the UI dynamically when a button is clicked.
keyPoints: Used in forms and dynamic components

quiz.question: Which hook is used to create state in functional components?
quiz.explanation: useState is used to create state variables.

chapters.title: Event Handling
chapters.description: Handling user interactions in React applications

pages.title: Introduction to Event Handling
pages.content: Event handling in React allows applications to respond to user actions such as clicks, typing, and form submissions. React events are similar to JavaScript events but use camelCase syntax and pass functions as event handlers.

quiz.question: How are event names written in React?
quiz.explanation: React uses camelCase event names like onClick.

pages.title: Handling Click Events
pages.content: Click events are commonly used to trigger actions when users interact with buttons or other clickable elements. React uses the onClick event handler to manage click events.

quiz.question: Which event handles button clicks?
quiz.explanation: onClick is used for click events.

pages.title: Handling Input Events
pages.content: React can handle user input using the onChange event. This event is triggered whenever the value of an input field changes.

quiz.question: Which event detects input value changes?
quiz.explanation: onChange detects changes in input fields.

pages.title: Passing Parameters to Event Handlers
pages.content: Sometimes event handlers require parameters. In React, parameters can be passed using arrow functions inside event handlers.

quiz.question: How can parameters be passed to event handlers?
quiz.explanation: Arrow functions allow parameters to be passed.

pages.title: Using the Event Object
pages.content: React passes an event object to event handlers. This object contains useful information about the event, such as the element that triggered the event and its value.

quiz.question: What does event.preventDefault() do?
quiz.explanation: preventDefault stops the browser's default action.

chapters.title: Conditional Rendering
chapters.description: Rendering UI elements based on conditions in React

pages.title: Introduction to Conditional Rendering
pages.content: Conditional rendering in React allows components to display different UI elements depending on certain conditions. It works similarly to conditional statements in JavaScript such as if statements and ternary operators.
keyPoints: Used to show or hide UI elements

quiz.question: What is conditional rendering used for?
quiz.explanation: Conditional rendering displays UI based on conditions.

pages.title: Using if Statements
pages.content: The simplest way to implement conditional rendering is by using if statements. Based on the condition, the component can return different JSX elements.

quiz.question: Which statement is commonly used for conditional rendering?
quiz.explanation: if statements are used to check conditions.

pages.title: Using Ternary Operator
pages.content: The ternary operator is a compact way to implement conditional rendering directly inside JSX. It allows developers to render one element if a condition is true and another if it is false.

quiz.question: Which operator is used for inline conditions?
quiz.explanation: The ternary operator (? :) handles inline conditions.

pages.title: Using Logical && Operator
pages.content: The logical AND (&&) operator is used to render elements only when a condition is true. If the condition is false, nothing is rendered.
keyPoints: Renders element only if condition is true

quiz.question: What happens if the condition is false with && operator?
quiz.explanation: If condition is false, React renders nothing.

pages.title: Conditional Rendering Example
pages.content: Below is an example where conditional rendering is used to show different messages based on login status.

quiz.question: Which hook is often used with conditional rendering?
quiz.explanation: useState is commonly used to manage conditions.

chapters.title: Lists and Keys
chapters.description: Rendering dynamic lists and understanding the importance of keys in React

pages.title: Rendering Lists in React
pages.content: React allows developers to render multiple elements dynamically using arrays. This is commonly done when displaying lists of data such as products, users, or blog posts.

quiz.question: Which function is commonly used to render lists in React?
quiz.explanation: map() is used to transform arrays into JSX elements.

pages.title: Using map() Function
pages.content: The map() function is used to transform each element in an array into a React element. It loops through the array and returns JSX for every item.

quiz.question: What does map() return in React lists?
quiz.explanation: map() returns JSX elements.

pages.title: Understanding Keys
pages.content: Keys are special attributes used by React to identify elements in a list. They help React determine which items have changed, been added, or removed. This improves performance during rendering.

quiz.question: Why are keys used in React lists?
quiz.explanation: Keys help React track changes in list elements.

pages.title: Best Practices for Keys
pages.content: Keys should always be unique and stable. Instead of using array indexes, developers should use unique IDs whenever possible to prevent unexpected UI behavior.

quiz.question: Which value is best for React keys?
quiz.explanation: Unique IDs are the best choice for keys.

pages.title: List Rendering Example
pages.content: Below is an example where a list of products is dynamically rendered using the map() function and unique keys.

quiz.question: Which method helps render dynamic lists?
quiz.explanation: map() renders array items as JSX elements.

chapters.title: Forms in React
chapters.description: Handling user input and form submission in React applications

pages.title: Introduction to Forms
pages.content: Forms in React are used to collect user input such as names, emails, and passwords. React manages form data using state. This approach allows developers to control how input values are handled and updated.
keyPoints: React manages form data using state

quiz.question: What are forms used for in React?
quiz.explanation: Forms are used to collect user input.

pages.title: Controlled Components
pages.content: Controlled components are form elements whose values are controlled by React state. Every time the user types something, the state is updated using an event handler.
keyPoints: Form inputs controlled by React state

quiz.question: What controls the value of a controlled component?
quiz.explanation: Controlled components use React state.

pages.title: Handling Multiple Inputs
pages.content: When forms have multiple input fields, developers can manage them using a single state object. This approach simplifies form management.
keyPoints: Multiple inputs can share one state object

quiz.question: Which attribute helps identify form fields?
quiz.explanation: The name attribute identifies form fields.

pages.title: Handling Form Submission
pages.content: React handles form submission using the onSubmit event. Developers usually prevent the default browser behavior using event.preventDefault().

quiz.question: Which event handles form submission?
quiz.explanation: onSubmit handles form submission.

pages.title: Complete Form Example
pages.content: Below is a complete React form example where user input is stored in state and displayed when the form is submitted.

quiz.question: Which hook is commonly used in React forms?
quiz.explanation: useState manages form input values.

chapters.title: useEffect Hook
chapters.description: Handling side effects in React functional components

pages.title: Introduction to useEffect
pages.content: The useEffect hook allows React components to perform side effects. Side effects include operations such as data fetching, DOM manipulation, logging, or setting timers. useEffect runs after the component renders.
keyPoints: Replaces lifecycle methods in class components

quiz.question: What is the purpose of useEffect?
quiz.explanation: useEffect is used to handle side effects.

pages.title: Basic useEffect Example
pages.content: The useEffect hook runs after every render by default. It accepts a function that contains the code to run after the component updates.
keyPoints: Runs after every render by default
Commonly used for logging and data fetching

quiz.question: When does useEffect run by default?
quiz.explanation: useEffect runs after the component renders.

pages.title: Dependency Array
pages.content: The dependency array controls when useEffect runs. If an empty array is provided, the effect runs only once when the component mounts.

quiz.question: What does an empty dependency array mean?
quiz.explanation: An empty dependency array runs the effect once on mount.

pages.title: Fetching Data with useEffect
pages.content: useEffect is commonly used for fetching data from APIs. When the component loads, the effect can trigger an API call and update state with the response.

quiz.question: What is a common use of useEffect?
quiz.explanation: useEffect is commonly used for API calls.

pages.title: Cleanup Function
pages.content: Sometimes side effects need cleanup, such as clearing timers or removing event listeners. useEffect allows returning a cleanup function that runs when the component unmounts.

quiz.question: Why are cleanup functions used?
quiz.explanation: Cleanup functions prevent memory leaks.

chapters.title: useContext Hook
chapters.description: Sharing global data across React components using Context API

pages.title: Introduction to Context API
pages.content: The Context API allows React applications to share data between components without passing props manually through multiple levels. It is useful for global data such as user authentication, themes, and language settings.
pages.exampleCode:
import { createContext } from 'react';

const UserContext = createContext();
keyPoints: Avoids passing props through many components

quiz.question: What problem does Context API solve?
quiz.explanation: Context API helps avoid prop drilling.

pages.title: Creating a Context
pages.content: A context is created using the createContext() function. This context can then be used to share values between components.
pages.exampleCode:
import { createContext } from 'react';

export const ThemeContext = createContext();

quiz.question: Which function creates a context?
quiz.explanation: createContext() creates a React context.

pages.title: Using Context Provider
pages.content: The Provider component is used to wrap components that need access to the shared data. It supplies the context value to all child components.

quiz.question: Which component provides context values?
quiz.explanation: Provider supplies context values.

pages.title: Using useContext Hook
pages.content: The useContext hook allows components to access context values directly. It simplifies the process of consuming context compared to older methods.

quiz.question: Which hook reads context values?
quiz.explanation: useContext is used to access context values.

pages.title: Context Example
pages.content: Below is an example where a user name is shared globally across components using the Context API.

quiz.question: Which hook helps access global data from context?
quiz.explanation: useContext accesses context values.

chapters.title: React Router
chapters.description: Implementing client-side routing in React applications

pages.title: Introduction to React Router
pages.content: React Router is a library used to enable navigation between different components in a React application. It allows developers to build single-page applications with multiple views without reloading the page.
pages.exampleCode: npm install react-router-dom

quiz.question: Which library is used for routing in React?
quiz.explanation: react-router-dom is used for routing in React applications.

pages.title: BrowserRouter
pages.content: BrowserRouter is a component that enables routing in React applications. It uses the HTML5 history API to keep the UI in sync with the URL.

quiz.question: Which component enables routing in React apps?
quiz.explanation: BrowserRouter enables routing in React.

pages.title: Routes and Route
pages.content: Routes define which component should render based on the URL path. Each Route component maps a path to a specific React component.
keyPoints: Route renders a component for a URL

quiz.question: Which component defines a URL path?
quiz.explanation: Route defines which component loads for a path.

pages.title: Navigation using Link
pages.content: React Router provides the Link component for navigation between pages. Unlike traditional anchor tags, Link does not reload the page.

quiz.question: Which component is used for navigation?
quiz.explanation: Link navigates between pages without refreshing.

pages.title: Dynamic Routes
pages.content: Dynamic routes allow developers to create routes with parameters. These parameters can be accessed using the useParams hook.
keyPoints: Common in profile and product pages

quiz.question: Which hook reads dynamic route parameters?
quiz.explanation: useParams retrieves dynamic route values.

chapters.title: Custom Hooks
chapters.description: Creating reusable logic in React using custom hooks

pages.title: What are Custom Hooks?
pages.content: Custom Hooks are JavaScript functions that allow developers to reuse stateful logic across multiple React components. They follow the same rules as React hooks and must start with the word 'use'.

quiz.question: How should custom hooks start?
quiz.explanation: Custom hooks must start with 'use'.

pages.title: Why Use Custom Hooks?
pages.content: Custom hooks help avoid repeating the same logic across multiple components. They improve code readability and allow developers to separate business logic from UI logic.

quiz.question: Why are custom hooks useful?
quiz.explanation: Custom hooks help reuse logic across components.

pages.title: Creating a Custom Hook
pages.content: A custom hook is simply a JavaScript function that uses React hooks internally. Developers can create their own hooks to encapsulate reusable functionality.
keyPoints: Custom hooks use React hooks internally

quiz.question: What does a custom hook usually return?
quiz.explanation: Custom hooks usually return state values and functions.

pages.title: Using Custom Hooks
pages.content: Once created, custom hooks can be used inside React components just like built-in hooks. They help simplify component code.

quiz.question: Where can custom hooks be used?
quiz.explanation: Custom hooks are used inside React components.

pages.title: Custom Hook Example
pages.content: Below is an example of a custom hook that tracks window width and updates whenever the browser window is resized.
keyPoints: Custom hooks can manage complex logic

quiz.question: Which hook is often used inside custom hooks?
quiz.explanation: Custom hooks commonly use useState and useEffect.

chapters.title: Performance Optimization
chapters.description: Techniques to improve performance and prevent unnecessary re-renders in React applications

pages.title: Introduction to Performance Optimization
pages.content: Performance optimization in React focuses on improving application efficiency and preventing unnecessary component re-renders. Optimizing performance becomes important in large applications with complex components and frequent state updates.

quiz.question: Why is performance optimization important?
quiz.explanation: Performance optimization improves application speed and efficiency.

pages.title: React.memo
pages.content: React.memo is a higher-order component that prevents unnecessary re-rendering of functional components. It only re-renders a component when its props change.

quiz.question: What does React.memo do?
quiz.explanation: React.memo prevents unnecessary component re-renders.

pages.title: useMemo Hook
pages.content: The useMemo hook is used to memoize expensive calculations. It recomputes the value only when its dependencies change.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of useMemo?
quiz.explanation: useMemo memoizes expensive calculations.

pages.title: useCallback Hook
pages.content: The useCallback hook memoizes functions to prevent them from being recreated on every render. This is useful when passing functions to child components.

quiz.question: Which hook memoizes functions?
quiz.explanation: useCallback memoizes functions.

pages.title: Avoiding Unnecessary Re-renders
pages.content: Unnecessary re-renders can slow down React applications. Developers can optimize performance using techniques like React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback.

quiz.question: Which tool helps prevent unnecessary component renders?
quiz.explanation: React.memo prevents unnecessary component re-renders.

chapters.title: React Project Structure
chapters.description: Organizing React applications using a scalable and maintainable folder structure

pages.title: Why Project Structure Matters
pages.content: As React applications grow, organizing files becomes very important. A good project structure helps developers manage components, styles, utilities, and logic efficiently. It improves maintainability and teamwork in large projects.
pages.exampleCode:
src/
  components/
  pages/
  hooks/
  context/
  services/
  assets/

quiz.question: Why is project structure important?
quiz.explanation: A proper structure helps organize files and improve maintainability.

pages.title: Typical React Folder Structure
pages.content: A typical React application contains multiple folders that separate components, pages, hooks, and utilities. This separation improves scalability and readability.
pages.exampleCode:
src/
  components/
    Navbar.jsx
    Button.jsx
  pages/
    Home.jsx
    Dashboard.jsx
  hooks/
    useAuth.js
  services/
    api.js
  App.jsx
  main.jsx

quiz.question: Which folder usually stores reusable UI elements?
quiz.explanation: Reusable UI elements are stored in the components folder.

pages.title: Organizing Components
pages.content: Components should be organized based on their purpose. Small reusable components go into the components folder, while larger view-level components go into the pages folder.
pages.exampleCode:
components/
  Button.jsx
  Card.jsx

pages/
  Home.jsx
  Courses.jsx

quiz.question: Where should reusable components be stored?
quiz.explanation: Reusable components belong in the components folder.

pages.title: Separating Logic and UI
pages.content: React projects should separate business logic from UI components. Logic can be placed in custom hooks, services, or context providers.
pages.exampleCode:
hooks/
  useAuth.js

services/
  apiService.js

quiz.question: Where should API logic usually be stored?
quiz.explanation: API logic is commonly stored in services.

pages.title: Best Practices for Large Applications
pages.content: Large React applications should follow best practices such as modular components, reusable hooks, clear folder structure, and separation of concerns.
pages.exampleCode:
src/
  components/
  pages/
  hooks/
  context/
  services/
  utils/
  assets/
  styles/

quiz.question: Which practice improves React scalability?
quiz.explanation: Modular components improve scalability.

interviewQuestions.question: What is React?
interviewQuestions.answer: React is a JavaScript library used for building user interfaces using reusable components.

interviewQuestions.question: What are the main features of React?
interviewQuestions.answer: Component-based architecture, Virtual DOM, unidirectional data flow, reusable components, and strong ecosystem.

interviewQuestions.question: What is JSX?
interviewQuestions.answer: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It allows developers to write HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript.

interviewQuestions.question: What are React components?
interviewQuestions.answer: Components are reusable building blocks of a React application that return JSX to render UI.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between functional and class components?
interviewQuestions.answer: Functional components are JavaScript functions using hooks, while class components are ES6 classes using lifecycle methods.

interviewQuestions.question: What are props in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: Props are inputs passed from parent components to child components to display dynamic data.

interviewQuestions.question: Are props mutable or immutable?
interviewQuestions.answer: Props are immutable (read-only).

interviewQuestions.question: What is state in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: State is a built-in object that stores dynamic data and controls component behavior.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the useState hook?
interviewQuestions.answer: useState is a hook used to add state to functional components.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the Virtual DOM?
interviewQuestions.answer: Virtual DOM is a lightweight copy of the real DOM used by React to optimize UI updates.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between state and props?
interviewQuestions.answer: Props are passed from parent components, while state is managed inside a component.

interviewQuestions.question: What are React Hooks?
interviewQuestions.answer: Hooks are functions that allow developers to use state and lifecycle features in functional components.

interviewQuestions.question: What is useEffect used for?
interviewQuestions.answer: useEffect is used for performing side effects such as API calls, DOM updates, and timers.

interviewQuestions.question: What is prop drilling?
interviewQuestions.answer: Prop drilling is passing data through multiple component levels unnecessarily.

interviewQuestions.question: How can prop drilling be avoided?
interviewQuestions.answer: Using Context API or state management libraries like Redux.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the Context API?
interviewQuestions.answer: Context API allows sharing global data across components without passing props manually.

interviewQuestions.question: What is React Router?
interviewQuestions.answer: React Router is a library used for client-side routing in React applications.

interviewQuestions.question: What are keys in React lists?
interviewQuestions.answer: Keys are unique identifiers used to track list elements efficiently during rendering.

interviewQuestions.question: Why should keys be unique?
interviewQuestions.answer: Unique keys help React efficiently update and re-render only changed elements.

interviewQuestions.question: What are controlled components?
interviewQuestions.answer: Controlled components are form inputs whose values are managed by React state.

interviewQuestions.question: What are custom hooks?
interviewQuestions.answer: Custom hooks are reusable functions that encapsulate logic using React hooks.

interviewQuestions.question: What is React.memo?
interviewQuestions.answer: React.memo prevents unnecessary re-renders of functional components.

interviewQuestions.question: What is useMemo?
interviewQuestions.answer: useMemo memoizes expensive calculations to improve performance.

interviewQuestions.question: What is useCallback?
interviewQuestions.answer: useCallback memoizes functions to prevent unnecessary re-renders.

interviewQuestions.question: What is lazy loading in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: Lazy loading loads components only when needed using React.lazy.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Suspense in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: Suspense allows React to display fallback content while loading components.

interviewQuestions.question: What is reconciliation?
interviewQuestions.answer: Reconciliation is the process React uses to update the DOM efficiently.

interviewQuestions.question: What are Higher Order Components (HOC)?
interviewQuestions.answer: HOCs are functions that take a component and return an enhanced component.

interviewQuestions.question: What is code splitting?
interviewQuestions.answer: Code splitting divides the application bundle into smaller chunks for better performance.

interviewQuestions.question: What is server-side rendering (SSR)?
interviewQuestions.answer: SSR renders React components on the server instead of the browser.

interviewQuestions.question: What is hydration in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: Hydration attaches React functionality to server-rendered HTML.

interviewQuestions.question: What is React Fiber?
interviewQuestions.answer: React Fiber is the internal algorithm used for incremental rendering.

interviewQuestions.question: What are fragments in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: Fragments allow grouping multiple elements without adding extra DOM nodes.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the purpose of useRef?
interviewQuestions.answer: useRef provides a way to access DOM elements directly.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between useMemo and useCallback?
interviewQuestions.answer: useMemo memoizes values, while useCallback memoizes functions.

interviewQuestions.question: What is state lifting in React?
interviewQuestions.answer: State lifting means moving state to a common parent component.

interviewQuestions.question: What is conditional rendering?
interviewQuestions.answer: Conditional rendering displays UI elements based on conditions.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a single-page application (SPA)?
interviewQuestions.answer: SPA is a web app that loads a single HTML page and updates content dynamically.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the role of ReactDOM?
interviewQuestions.answer: ReactDOM renders React components to the browser DOM.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between React and Angular?
interviewQuestions.answer: React is a UI library, while Angular is a full framework.
